Maintenance Report — MNT-0107-002

Asset: WELL-0107 (NE-07 Well 107, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: wellhead Work started: 27 Jan 2023 08:00 · Finished: 31 Jan 2023 01:00 · Well stopped for this job: 89 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price, Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0107-0015 on 2023-01-26 Report written: 31 Jan 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw a thin film of oil on the wellhead. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0107-0015 showed the wellhead at 9.1 °C with the air at 10.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The packing rings were worn and the polished rod was lightly scored. The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Normal packing wear.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started, but it was not written down (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Closed the wellhead valves and bled off pressure.
  2. Removed the old packing.
  3. Installed new packing rings and adjusted the gland.
  4. Cleaned the wellhead area.

Summary of the fix: replaced stuffing box packing.

Testing and return to service

Checked the stuffing box with the unit running: no leak. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0107-006

Asset: WELL-0107 (NE-07 Well 107, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: rod string Work started: 09 Jul 2023 08:00 · Finished: 26 Jul 2023 12:00 · Well stopped for this job: 412 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0107-0038 on 2023-07-06 Report written: 26 Jul 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator noticed the pump jack running unusually light and no fluid reaching the flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0107-0038 showed the wellhead at 33.0 °C with the air at 33.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 15 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Fatigue failure of a rod body, probably started by corrosion pitting.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

Rod couplings1,191

Total16,997

Notes and recommendations

  • Consider corrosion inhibitor treatment for this well.
  • Keep the recovered rod for failure analysis.

maintenance.action: Replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil

Maintenance Report — MNT-0107-009

Asset: WELL-0107 (NE-07 Well 107, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 27 Oct 2023 08:00 · Finished: 07 Nov 2023 21:00 · Well stopped for this job: 277 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0107-0054 on 2023-10-26 Report written: 09 Nov 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that oil was dripping from the gearbox onto the pump jack base. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0107-0054 showed the wellhead at 29.7 °C with the air at 19.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 10 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Seal wear, made worse by heat and a low oil level.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0107-009 (WS-06).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0107-019

Asset: WELL-0107 (NE-07 Well 107, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 25 Apr 2025 08:00 · Finished: 29 Apr 2025 00:00 · Well stopped for this job: 88 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price, Daniel Foster · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0107-0132 on 2025-04-24 Report written: 30 Apr 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid stopped reaching the flowline and the rod load spiked on the downstroke. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0107-0132 showed the wellhead at 26.7 °C with the air at 21.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 2 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Sand and scale build-up in the pump barrel.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.

maintenance.action: Replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0107-020

Asset: WELL-0107 (NE-07 Well 107, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 30 May 2025 08:00 · Finished: 31 May 2025 04:00 · Well stopped for this job: 20 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0107-0137 on 2025-05-29 Report written: 31 May 2025

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0107-0137 at 07:15 on 2025-05-29 found crude oil on the pad: about 7.3% of the pad area, estimated 1.9 bbl. The inspector noted: "Dark staining on pad." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.8 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Thread fatigue from pump jack vibration.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 1% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 296 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 237 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 2.6 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0107-020 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.25% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Absorbents and berms782

Labour (company crew and contractor)2,011
Total5,923

Notes and recommendations

  • Record the leak location for the flowline maintenance program (RC-05).
